# Deleted terminal bundles leave no executable loader dependency

Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e

## TLDR

Considered whether removing the bundles leaves terminals waiting forever for scripts that no longer ship. Source checks refute that failure route.

## Details

The assigned deletions remove xterm.js, addon-fit.js, addon-clipboard.js and portions of addon-unicode-graphemes.js. In the same commit, crates/farhelm-ui/src/lib.rs removes their asset declarations; lines 1914–1926 load the grid helpers and terminal.js instead. assets/terminal.js:3203–3229 gates mounting only on the shipped grid/helpers/fonts, and :4303–4350 constructs window.farhelmGridTerminal.create. A pinned git grep across crates, e2e and scripts for the deleted asset paths and add-on global names found only historical explanatory comments and retained ported-code attribution, no executable use.

Contract: SPEC_impl.md:1504–1514 states, ‘Every terminal runs in a terminal host’ and ‘the browser draws a grid stream with its own grid client’; :1843–1846 states terminal.js ‘mounts the grid component for every terminal before the socket exists’. This is a source-based conclusion, not an executed mount check.

Suggested bucket: high/material UX if the suspected mount failure existed; no defect established. Confidence: confirmed refutation for the removed script/global dependency. proposed_drop: executable asset declarations, script injection and readiness predicates were migrated together; there is no remaining loader dependency on these deleted bundles. possible_cover: none; coverage sources not consulted. Could-be-highest: no; the considered consequence is an unavailable terminal display, with no established route to loss of work or security impact. Caveat: this checks deletion integration, not every behavior of the grid replacement.

## TLDR

Considered whether deleting the fit add-on prevents terminals from fitting their panes. The replacement already measures and reports terminal dimensions without the add-on.

## Details

The removed addon-fit.js:1 implements fit/proposeDimensions from container dimensions, cell dimensions, padding and a scrollbar reserve. This is direct source evidence of an independent replacement, not observed runtime behavior.

The fixed 80-column/24-row proposal reference deliberately differs from continually feeding committed dimensions back into fit; deletion of the upstream fit code does not violate that contract.

# Grid fit also handles mounting before its socket exists

Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e

## TLDR

The deleted fit add-on is replaced by grid sizing. Synthesis also checked whether fitting before socket creation can throw or lose the initial dimensions; the caller explicitly handles that ordering.

## Details

The original removal concern remains refuted. assets/grid-terminal.js:217–246 supplies cellFor/proposeSize, including the scrollbar reserve and minimum 2 by 1 size; :473–504 measures and invokes onResize. assets/terminal.js:3389–3394 constructs the grid, calls fit and obtains the size before making the socket; :4319 supplies sendResize. SPEC_impl.md:1847–1854 states, ‘The grid's deterministic fit is Farhelm's documented formula’ and ‘they are Farhelm's fit contract now’. The fixed 80-column/24-row proposal reference is intentional.

The synthesis lifecycle check read terminal.js:3251–3320 and :4555–4571. ws is initialized to null outside the try block before constructing the surface. sendResize is a hoisted function whose first condition returns while ws is absent or not OPEN, before it reads grid.size(). The constructor's early callback therefore cannot dereference a missing socket or the not-yet-assigned grid. The mount reads size after construction for the attach URL; the documented onopen path sends current size again to cover changes between construction and connection. This resolves the cross-batch assumption that fitting remains safe when all terminals now create the grid before any socket.

Suggested bucket: high/material UX if pane sizing or initial mounting failed; no such defect established. Confidence: confirmed source refutation. proposed_drop: replacement measurement and callers remain present, and explicit null/open checks make the pre-socket resize callback safe. possible_cover: none; coverage sources not consulted. Could-be-highest: no; neither this lifecycle concern nor the original missing-fit concern establishes loss of work or security impact. Caveat: source-only analysis; no numerical fit tests or browser execution occurred, and exhaustive sizing edge cases remain outside this removal check.

# Clipboard add-on removal retains write delivery and read refusal

Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e

## TLDR

Considered whether removing the clipboard add-on loses terminal copying or exposes clipboard contents to terminal programs. The grid has its own write path and the supervisor refuses reads before anything reaches the page.

## Details

The removed add-on parses OSC 52 and can read through a configured provider. Its removal also removes the need for that browser-side provider's read override: crates/farhelm-terminal-emulator/src/emulator.rs:103 fixes Osc52::OnlyCopy for every new emulator, and :118–125 constructs the terminal with that configuration. effects.rs:173–195 converts ClipboardStore to a write effect but discards ClipboardLoad, and :207–211 emits writes only from live output. The queries.rs:360–362 handler delegates to the copy-only terminal. A pinned search locates the enforcing read guard in vendor/alacritty_terminal/src/term/mod.rs:2210–2211, whose predicate admits OnlyPaste or CopyPaste, neither of which the emulator configures.

The UI side remains independent of the removed add-on: assets/grid-terminal.js:1975–1983 applies the frame and forwards takeClipboard results; assets/terminal.js:4326–4333 sends system-clipboard writes and completed local selections to enqueueClipboardWrite; :764–773 selects the native bridge or navigator.clipboard.writeText.

Contract: SPEC.md:3063–3065 says ‘an OSC 52 READ is never answered with clipboard contents’ and that user paste ‘does not authorize a program to query the clipboard’. SPEC_impl.md:1732–1734 requires the two page write paths to use the shared native-first writer; :1746 says ‘the native route is write-only by construction’. The source paths above preserve these boundaries.

Suggested bucket: highest/security for the considered clipboard disclosure route, high/material UX for missing writes; neither defect established. Confidence: confirmed source refutation for deletion of the browser add-on weakening these boundaries. proposed_drop: the replacement's explicit copy-only emulator configuration and discarded read events refute disclosure, while independent grid write callbacks refute loss of the handler. possible_cover: none; coverage sources not consulted. Could-be-highest: yes, disclosure of clipboard secrets would be security-impacting, but no shipped read route exists in the checked source. This is source analysis only, with no runtime clipboard execution. Caveat: the review checks removal integration, not every clipboard queue or permission-policy edge case.

# Clipboard removal preserves its boundary; primary-notice gap predates the range

Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e

## TLDR

The deleted add-on leaves an independent system-clipboard write path and does not expose clipboard contents to programs. Synthesis found that a program writing only its primary selection can still receive incorrect ‘copied nothing’ drag guidance, but both sides of that mismatch already existed before this review's exclusive base. It is not a defect introduced by the assigned deletion.

## Details

The original security concern remains refuted: crates/farhelm-terminal-emulator/src/emulator.rs:103 configures Osc52::OnlyCopy, vendor/alacritty_terminal/src/term/mod.rs:2210–2213 returns without processing clipboard reads under that configuration, and effects.rs:173–195 discards ClipboardLoad as well. Source-checked system writes remain wired through effects.rs:207–208, hosts/terminal.rs:3310–3321, service/handlers.rs:1907–1915, service/grid_stream.rs:844–849, assets/grid-terminal.js:1975–1983, and assets/terminal.js:4326–4333 and :764–773. The shared page writer selects the native bridge or navigator.clipboard.writeText. SPEC.md:3063–3065 says ‘an OSC 52 READ is never answered with clipboard contents’ and user paste ‘does not authorize a program to query the clipboard’; SPEC_impl.md:1732–1746 specifies the shared native-first write path. No read route was found.

Synthesis checked the full primary-write caller assumption rather than relying on the UI callback's comment. hosts/terminal.rs:3310–3321 only broadcasts ClipboardTarget::Clipboard; service/grid_stream.rs:844–849 independently filters to that same target. The actual attachment in service/handlers.rs:1907–1915 uses terminal.subscribe_notices(), so there is no alternative primary-notice route in that attachment. Consequently the primary target never reaches terminal.js:4326–4330 to increment its program-copy counter. This can cause false drag-copy guidance when only a primary-selection write follows a program-owned drag. SPEC.md:3074–3075 explicitly requires ‘Any completed program clipboard write, including a primary-selection write, suppresses it during the grace window.’ The initial c3 conclusion covers actual system copying and read refusal; it must not be read as establishing that every primary write reaches the page.

The provenance check settles scope: at exclusive base 6e423e30068b62c6cfa276c6d720ee35bb70387a, hosts/terminal.rs:3210–3221 already has the identical clipboard-only broadcast predicate, and terminal.js:6012–6016 already counts delivered targets while :6113–6124 bases the grace notice on that count. The reviewed commit's parent has the same service/grid_stream.rs:844–849 filter. The reviewed hosts/terminal.rs diff only removes wire_kind/tab_info methods, leaving notice delivery unchanged. No retired implementation defect was investigated. The replacement's pre-existing omission does not result from deleting these vendor bundles.

# Unicode add-on removal does not remove the grid's width authority

Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e

## TLDR

Considered whether removing the browser's Unicode provider makes emoji and combining characters move later terminal columns. The replacement receives widths from the supervisor and draws each non-ASCII cell at that declared width; it does not call the removed provider.

## Details

The assigned addon-unicode-graphemes.js packets include its charProperties delegation, UnicodeService and constructor/helper code, all deleted at this commit. No independent defect in these retired helpers was sought. The replacement source at assets/grid-model.js:1174–1190 treats non-ASCII run text as one cell's content at the transmitted width. assets/grid-terminal.js:759–779 calls layoutRun(shown, run.width), places non-flow text in boxes of cells * cellWidth pixels, and advances the next column by run.width. It does not compute terminal widths with the removed UnicodeService or add-on. Pinned searches for UnicodeGraphemesAddon and the deleted bundle name found no executable consumer remaining.

Contract: SPEC_impl.md:1839–1842 says the supervisor interprets the terminal and the browser ‘gets the screen and scrollback as rows of styled runs’ and ‘is not a terminal emulator’. Its complete supervisor-emulator section (:2672–2731) names alacritty_terminal plus Farhelm policy as the interpretation authority and specifies its variation-selector behavior; the old browser provider's Unicode 15 grapheme rules are not the width authority of this stream. This refutation rests on the concrete replacement layout path and contract, not an assumption that every old/new Unicode behavior matches.

Confidence: confirmed source refutation for deletion removing the active provider. proposed_drop: the provider belonged to the retired browser emulator, whereas the active renderer uses supervisor-declared widths and retained box layout. possible_cover: none; coverage sources not consulted. Could-be-highest: no; no security or loss-of-work route follows from this considered missing-width-provider concern. Caveat: no browser rendering or Unicode parity execution was performed, and pre-existing emulator width defects unrelated to removal remain outside this assignment.

Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e; exclusive base checked at 6e423e30068b62c6cfa276c6d720ee35bb70387a.

## TLDR

A program that handles a drag by writing only its primary selection can still receive incorrect guidance saying that it copied nothing. Both this source mismatch and the promise it violates already existed before the reviewed range. This record separates that known guidance consequence from c3's original, refuted clipboard-confidentiality concern; it is not new discovery.

## Details

Preserved synthesis source: at the reviewed commit, hosts/terminal.rs:3310–3321 filters notices to ClipboardTarget::Clipboard; service/grid_stream.rs:844–849 independently does the same. service/handlers.rs:1907–1915 supplies terminal.subscribe_notices() to the actual grid attachment. The primary write therefore cannot reach terminal.js:4326–4330 to increment gridOsc52Writes, and :4426–4431 admits the false guidance after the grace window. Current SPEC.md:3074–3075 requires ‘Any completed program clipboard write, including a primary-selection write, suppresses it during the grace window.’ This is a real source/contract mismatch, not refuted by correct system clipboard writing or read refusal.

The caller's g186/c2:7 question is now settled at the whole-range boundary, not only the immediate parent. At exclusive base, hosts/terminal.rs:3210–3221 already has the identical clipboard-only broadcast, terminal.js:6012–6016 already counts only delivered callbacks, and :6113–6124 has the same guidance condition. Thus an in-range new primary-write requirement does not explain this mismatch. The reviewed commit's parent has the same service/grid_stream.rs:844–849 filter, and its terminal.js grid counter is unchanged by the reviewed deletion. The raw old-terminal counter formerly handled this separately; deleting that retired path does not newly introduce the live grid's omission.

# Removing bundle notices does not orphan retained ported-code notices

Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e. Discovery pass 1.

## TLDR

Checked whether deleting xterm and fit bundles and their companion notices also deletes the only shipped attribution for code retained in the replacement renderer. Source shows that the replacement has an independent notice asset that remains declared. No omission found.

## Details

The reviewed THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md diff deletes the section for whole npm bundles but retains ‘Code ported from xterm.js’, explicitly pointing to assets/grid-ported-code-LICENSES.txt. That file's reviewed content retains complete xterm, fit, web-links and Visual Studio Code notices. Its content lists the retained code and does not depend on deleted files for the notice text. crates/farhelm-ui/src/lib.rs:1484–1495 keeps GRID_PORTED_CODE_LICENSES with #[used] and asset!("/assets/grid-ported-code-LICENSES.txt", AssetOptions::builder().with_hash_suffix(false)). Its declaration is independent of the removed vendor asset constants. This refutes the specific source hypothesis that the assigned bundle deletion removes the sole declaration or text of notices for the retained ports; it does not claim an executed distribution audit.

Source-declared contract: retained THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md states ‘The complete notices are in crates/farhelm-ui/assets/grid-ported-code-LICENSES.txt’ and that it ‘ships in the app’; the actual declaration and file remain present at the reviewed commit.

Suggested bucket: other for a hypothetical missing attribution artifact; no source defect established. Confidence: confirmed source refutation of removal orphaning these retained notices. proposed_drop: independent complete notice file and retained asset declaration refute the considered removal consequence. possible_cover: none; no prohibited coverage sources searched, and supplied interface findings contain no notice-removal finding. Could-be-highest: no established security or user-work-loss consequence. Material caveats: no legal conclusion, no build, and no runtime/distribution inspection. This is a rejected candidate, not a new verified or unverified finding.
